video.title: Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft Pick 9 - Copper Flagg Ascension

summary: Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team, 9-category head-to-head snake mock draft from pick 9. He takes Cooper Flagg first because Flagg's worst case is still around 16th overall. His team after that: LaMelo Ball, Domantas Sabonis, Jalen Brunson, Franz Wagner, Ryan Rollins, Jarrett Allen, Norman Powell, Jalen Green, Kevin Porter Jr., Jeremiah Fears and Jake LaRavia. He says the build did not come together well. He regrets passing on Kel'el Ware and Collin Murray-Boyles, and says Brunson at that spot was probably not the best move. He sees a big group of undervalued players in the 30 to 70 range and says a balanced auction build lets you get several of them. His closing advice: stay flexible, win leagues with huge value picks, avoid reaching far ahead of a player's realistic range, and aim for upside first, then safety.

rules.text: When taking a player early, think about downside risk. If his worst case is still a decent finish, the pick is safe.
rules.quote: If you take Cooper Flag at nine, how bad's he going to be? Like, is he going to be 50th?

rules.text: The speaker says the sophomore slump is not a thing. Players historically improve in year two.
rules.quote: there is enough in Cooper Flag historical improvements into year two. No, sophomore slump is not a thing.

rules.text: Draft injury-risk players later in category leagues. He would take Kawhi Leonard in round three in roto but round four in category leagues.
rules.quote: In a Roto League, I would take him in round three. In a points league, I would take him in round four.

rules.text: In auctions, a balanced build lets you buy many undervalued mid-round players instead of spending big on early picks.
rules.quote: That's why I really love the balanced build in an auction is that these are all the guys

rules.text: The 30 to 70 range holds a lot of value. There are many players there the speaker likes.
rules.quote: there's like 50 guys, 40 guys in this 30 to 60 range or 30 to 70 range that I just like

rules.text: In late rounds, take upside flyers on players with uncertain roles.
rules.quote: We're just We're just hitting upside picks.

rules.text: Play in deeper leagues than 13 roster spots. The waiver wire will not run dry.
rules.quote: to say that the waiver wire is going to be dry is just not true. I guarantee you it's not true.

rules.text: Do not copy a set plan for a draft slot. Have several alternatives and adjust to who is available.
rules.quote: Do not look at my pick at number nine and go, "This is what I'm doing at pick nine."

rules.text: The gap between the 50th and 70th player is small. Leagues are won by huge values and lost to injuries or picks made 50 spots too early.
rules.quote: You win leagues by getting huge values, hundreds into 40s. You lose leagues a lot by luck, through injuries

rules.text: Aim for upside. If you cannot find upside, aim for safety.
rules.quote: Aim for upside and if you can't find the upside, aim for safety.

rules.text: Players who are inconsistent and sometimes bad get benched. Expect that when you draft them.
rules.quote: This is why there's no consistent role. This is why he's not locked in as a starter.
